gloss: snack (to go with drinks); knob; pinch

definitions.gloss: snack to accompany alcohol; drinking snack
definitions.explanation: Small dishes or finger food eaten while drinking alcohol. Synonymous with 肴 (さかな) and おつまみ (the polite form). A central concept in Japanese drinking culture.
A small protruding part that is grasped and turned or pulled, such as a volume knob or lid handle. From the verb つまむ (to pinch, to pick up).

examples.japanese: つまみを{注文|ちゅうもん}しよう。
{枝豆|えだまめ}はビールのつまみに{最高|さいこう}だ。
examples.english: Edamame is the perfect snack to go with beer.

examples.japanese: {居酒屋|いざかや}で{飲|の}みながら、いろいろなつまみを{楽|たの}しんだ。
examples.english: We enjoyed various snacks while drinking at the izakaya.

examples.japanese: ラジオのつまみを{回|まわ}す。
{鍋|なべ}の{蓋|ふた}のつまみが{熱|あつ}い。
examples.english: The knob on the pot lid is hot.

examples.japanese: {音量|おんりょう}のつまみを{左|ひだり}に{回|まわ}して{音|おと}を{小|ちい}さくした。
examples.english: I turned the volume knob to the left to lower the sound.

notes:
USAGE:
The polite form おつまみ is commonly used by customers when ordering. In casual speech, つまみ is standard. Both {酒|さけ}のつまみ and {酒|さけ}の{肴|さかな} mean "food to go with drinks," but つまみ is more casual.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- おつまみ (polite form — used when ordering)
- {酒|さけ}のつまみ (snack to accompany sake/alcohol)
- つまみになる (to serve as a drinking snack — also figurative: to become a topic of conversation)
- つまみを{回|まわ}す (to turn a knob)
- つまみ{食|ぐ}い (snacking; picking at food before it's served)
